rows.title: Is the UK open for business?
rows.standfirst: Globalization, as we once knew it, is dead ... well, that's according to the UK's new Chancellor of the Exchequer, Rachel Reeves.

rows.title: Chemicals found at the home of a Taylor Swift concert attack suspect, officials say
rows.standfirst: The suspect had uploaded an oath of allegiance to the current leader of the Islamic State militia group to an internet account a few weeks ago, investigators said Wednesday.

rows.title: 'Midwestern Nice' and 'Fun Dad' posts abound after Tim Walz is named VP pick
rows.standfirst: Walz's Midwestern-dad humor has endeared Harris supporters to the Minnesota governor and father of two, whose national visibility has been on the rise since Harris took over the Democratic ticket.

rows.title: The debate at the heart of new electricity transmission
rows.standfirst: The U.S. wants to become a net-zero emissions economy by 2050. That will mean a lot of new generation from renewable energy. It also means more transmission networks are needed to bring it onto the grid.

rows.title: U.S. lawmakers urge banning weighted infant sleepwear over safety concerns
rows.standfirst: Weighted infant sleepwear companies say their products are safe and help babies sleep, but some medical experts, safe-sleep advocates and government regulators warn the garments could be dangerous.

rows.title: 4 reasons why labor unions love Tim Walz
rows.standfirst: To labor advocates, Minnesota is considered one of the best places in America to be a worker. Last year, the Democratic legislature passed and Gov. Walz signed a sweeping package of pro-labor laws.

rows.title: The self-proclaimed GOAT of cybersquatting sold HarrisWalz.com for $15k
rows.standfirst: Jeremy Green Eche of Brooklyn buys and saves websites for hypothetical presidential tickets. On Tuesday, he sold HarrisWalz.com to a person seemingly unconnected to either campaign.

rows.title: The owners of a Colorado funeral home are ordered to pay $950M over mishandled remains
rows.standfirst: "Bad behavior has significant consequences,” the attorney representing families in a class-action lawsuit says. The remains of nearly 200 people were found at the Return to Nature Funeral Home.

rows.title: Google loses in antitrust lawsuit. And, Harris to announce VP pick
rows.standfirst: Google says it plans to appeal the ruling in an antitrust lawsuit that calls the company a monopoly. And, Harris to announce her running mate today in Philadelphia.

rows.title: 10 reasons why AI may be overrated
rows.standfirst: A list of reasons why generative AI may be overhyped.

rows.title: Meet the man with the plan to tax the world's wealthiest 3,000 people
rows.standfirst: The Brazilian government has proposed a 2% global wealth tax on the uber-rich. It would impact the 3,000 wealthiest people in the world.

rows.title: Google is defiant after losing antitrust lawsuit and being called a 'monopolist'
rows.standfirst: A federal judge rules that Google illegally abused its monopoly power to maintain its control over the search engine business. Google says it's appealing.

rows.title: Prosecutors say they plan to charge former police chief over Kansas newspaper raid
rows.standfirst: Prosecutors concluded that the staff at the Marion County Record committed no crimes before former Marion Police Chief Gideon Cody led a raid on its offices and the home of its publisher.

rows.title: Wally Amos, creator of Famous Amos cookies, has died
rows.standfirst: The creator of the grocery store snack aisle staple died at 88. His family said in a statement that he had dementia.

rows.title: Should presidents have more of a say in interest rates?
rows.standfirst: Former President Donald Trump recently suggested that if elected in this year's presidential election he would want more say on decisions made by the Federal Reserve. Presidents taking a more active role in monetary policy would mark an extraordinary shift in U.S. economic institutions, and mark the end of central bank independence.

rows.title: AI is changing video games — and striking performers want their due
rows.standfirst: Performers are on strike against major video game companies, and AI is the sticking point. Here’s how game development has evolved since early animation.

rows.title: Disney backtracks on request to toss wrongful death suit over Disney+ agreement
rows.standfirst: Jeffrey Piccolo's wife died after eating at a Disney World restaurant. Disney wanted his claims handled out of court based on the terms of his years-old Disney+ trial, but reversed its position.

rows.title: Meta shutters tool used to fight disinformation, despite outcry
rows.standfirst: The social media company discontinues its CrowdTangle tool, which researchers have used to track misinformation. Amid fears of election interference, lawmakers have urged Meta to keep it running.

rows.title: Rooftop solar has a fraud problem. The industry is working to build back trust
rows.standfirst: The rooftop solar business is a big source of consumer complaints. Across the country, prosecutors are investigating sales practices and financing arrangements. Now the solar industry is working to repair its reputation.

rows.title: Thinking about rooftop solar? 4 things to consider and how to protect yourself
rows.standfirst: The rooftop solar business is a big source of consumer complaints. The industry is working to repair its reputation. Here’s how you can protect yourself.

rows.title: Texas judge steps aside in Elon Musk's X case against advertisers
rows.standfirst: U.S. District Judge Reed O’Connor had been overseeing two cases filed by Musk’s social media platform X. Records showed O’Connor was also an investor in Tesla, another Musk company, as well as Unilever, a defendant in the Musk case.

rows.title: Sick of customer service bots and subscription headaches? There's a plan for that
rows.standfirst: This week, the Biden administration announced it is taking on more of what it calls "everyday headaches and hassles that waste Americans' time and money."

rows.title: The Denver basic income experiment
rows.standfirst: Homelessness is a pervasive issue that cities across the country struggle to address. This led an entrepreneur to team up with researchers and local foundations for an experiment called the Denver Basic Income Project. The goal was to see how different variations of a basic income program would impact the local homeless population. What the researchers found could become a guide for how localities in the United States could address the problem of homelessness.

rows.title: Former police chief faces a felony charge in the raid of a Kansas newspaper
rows.standfirst: The former Marion police chief is charged with felony obstruction of justice and is accused of persuading a potential witness for a probe into his conduct of withholding information from authorities.

rows.title: The Economic Mind of Tim Walz
rows.standfirst: A rundown on some of the Democratic VP candidate’s important economic policy decisions.

rows.title: Beach reads with a side of economics
rows.standfirst: It's that time of year when we want to lie on a beach and lose ourselves in a good book. Today on the show, three summer reading recs that got our hosts thinking about economics. Remember, anything read on the beach is, in fact, a "beach read."

rows.title: Costco says it's going to start cracking down on membership sharing
rows.standfirst: The retail giant says shoppers will soon have to start scanning their membership cards at the entrances to Costco warehouses rather than just presenting them to a store employee.

rows.title: What is the deal with car rentals?
rows.standfirst: Like several aspects of the travel economy, renting a car is more expensive than it was before the pandemic. Today on the show, we explore the great reset happening in the U.S. rental car industry that's kept prices elevated, left fleets leaner, and customers frustrated.

rows.title: Summer School 7: The Great Depression, the New Deal and how it changed our economy
rows.standfirst: Find all the episodes from this season here. And past seasons here. And follow along on TikTok here for video Summer School.

rows.title: Ford scraps all-electric SUV plan, saying drivers want hybrids
rows.standfirst: Ford will write down hundreds of millions of dollars because of the pivot. A key reason for the change, an analyst tells NPR, is that big batteries bring big costs.

rows.title: What's Zyn, and why there was a shortage this summer
rows.standfirst: Zyn pouches are the latest nicotine craze in the world of cigarette substitutes, with over 130 million containers sold in the first quarter of this year. Health experts and lawmakers are concerned.

rows.title: Jon Stewart doesn't feel vindicated bringing 'The Daily Show' to a Harris-led DNC
rows.standfirst: Stewart and The Daily Show 's executive producer Jennifer Flanz say the show is "clicking" with correspondents in the host chair. Is that a sustainable format for the late night comedy show? They'll revisit that question after the DNC.

rows.title: U.S. added fewer jobs in the past year than initially reported
rows.standfirst: A preliminary report from the Labor Department shows U.S. employers added 818,000 fewer jobs in the year ending in March than initially reported. The news comes during an election season in which the economy is a key issue.

rows.title: Federal judge throws out U.S. ban on noncompetes
rows.standfirst: A federal judge in Texas has struck down the government's ban on noncompetes. An estimated 30 million U.S. workers are subject to the employment agreements.

rows.title: Divers find 5 bodies during search of yacht wreckage off Sicily
rows.standfirst: The search continued for one more missing passenger on a yacht that sank off Sicily and questions intensified about why the vessel went down so quickly when a nearby sailboat remained largely unscathed.

rows.title: So, how's this No Tax On Tips thing gonna go?
rows.standfirst: By now, you've probably heard a lot from both presidential nominees about getting rid of taxes on tips.

rows.title: Who are Mike Lynch and the other people missing after a yacht sank in Sicily?
rows.standfirst: Lynch, a tech entrepreneur, had recently been acquitted on federal fraud charges in the U.S. The yacht he was on, the Bayesian, sank two days after Lynch's co-defendant was killed by a car.

rows.title: The White House plan to stop companies from wasting our time
rows.standfirst: The Biden-Harris administration has a new initiative called "Time Is Money."

rows.title: These Swifties are out thousands of dollars — but there's no 'bad blood' for Taylor
rows.standfirst: More than 150,000 fans lost their chance to see the pop superstar this month, due to terrorist threats. Now they mostly want another opportunity to see her in concert.

rows.title: Is endless vacation a scam?
rows.standfirst: Unlimited paid time off may sound like a nice perk, but it's not always what it appears. Employers aren't typically obligated to pay out unused vacation balances when a worker leaves, and it can be hard for workers to understand just how much time they can actually take off.

rows.title: Pioneer talk show host Phil Donahue dies at 88
rows.standfirst: The broadcaster was hailed as the father of the modern audience-participation daytime talk show. Donahue's taste for controversial and polarizing subjects birthed a new genre of television.

rows.title: Need a U.S. visa? You better have at least 677 days, some World Cup fans are learning
rows.standfirst: Many fans are dreaming of coming to the U.S. for the World Cup in 2026. One major problem looms: Wait times to get visas can be about two years for some.

rows.title: Over 17 million airline passengers head out for the busiest Labor Day weekend ever
rows.standfirst: This weekend caps a record-breaking season for travel, and those hitting the road will find lower gas prices than they did last year.

rows.title: How to fix a housing shortage
rows.standfirst: When Cody Fischer decided to get into real estate development, he had a vision. He wanted to build affordable, energy efficient apartments in Minneapolis, not far from where he grew up.

rows.title: Let's party like it's NVIDIA earnings report day!
rows.standfirst: On this Indicators of the Week, we take you to a Manhattan bar to watch NVIDIA's latest earnings reports. Plus, how publishers are trying to keep their books in Florida school libraries and what private equity is doing in Football.

rows.title: Brazil starts blocking social media platform X amid a dispute with Elon Musk
rows.standfirst: A Brazilian Supreme Court justice has ordered the suspension of Elon Musk's social media giant X in Brazil after the tech billionaire refused to name a legal representative in the country.

rows.title: A bill to protect performers from unauthorized AI heads to California governor
rows.standfirst: California Assembly Bill 2602 would regulate the use of generative AI for performers – not only those on-screen in films, TV and streaming series but also audiobooks and video games.

rows.title: A Hong Kong court convicts 2 journalists in a landmark sedition case
rows.standfirst: The editors had pleaded not guilty to conspiracy to publish and reproduce seditious publications. They face up to two years in prison and a fine. They were given bail pending sentencing on Sept. 26.

rows.title: The Olympian to influencer pipeline
rows.standfirst: While the 2024 Paris Olympics are over for some athletes, many competitors are still seeking to capitalize on their fame back on their college campuses. Thanks to the NCAA's 2021 rule changes for Name, Image and Likeness, college athletes are now able to leverage their stardom to maximize their earning potential.

rows.title: Best of Life Kit: Tips on how to deal with cheaters, cut food costs and split baby care
rows.standfirst: A roundup of eight useful tips from Life Kit's August episodes. This month's edition includes a sweet goodbye ritual for children and advice on how to save more money at the grocery store.

rows.title: Backpage founder Michael Lacey sentenced to 5 years in prison for money laundering
rows.standfirst: Michael Lacey, a founder of the classified site Backpage.com, was sentenced to five years in prison and fined $3 million in a money laundering case in a case involving allegations of sex trafficking.

rows.title: Summer School 8: Big ideas and life lessons from Marx, Keynes and Smith and more
rows.standfirst: Take the 2024 Planet Money Summer School Quiz here to earn your personalized diploma!

rows.title: How mortgage interest rates work (and why they're currently out of whack)
rows.standfirst: Even with falling interest rates in recent weeks, mortgage rates are still higher than you'd expect.

rows.title: Former elected official found guilty of murdering Las Vegas veteran reporter
rows.standfirst: An elected official in Las Vegas blamed his 2022 primary defeat on negative stories in the local newspaper. Now a jury has found him guilty of murdering the journalist who wrote them.

rows.title: Telegram CEO Pavel Durov indicted in France
rows.standfirst: The Russian-born tech billionaire was arrested by French authorities on Saturday. Prosecutors in Paris had been questioning him in connection with an investigation focused on drug trafficking

rows.title: What Biden’s tariffs on Chinese EVs and other products mean for U.S. consumers, jobs
rows.standfirst: President Biden and former President Donald Trump have both embraced tariffs on foreign imports. We asked economist Sanjay Patnaik of the nonpartisan Brookings Institution what tariffs on Chinese electric vehicles and other products mean for the U.S.

rows.standfirst: Time to show your economic history skills based on what we’ve covered in Planet Money Summer School 2024: An Incomplete Economic History of the World. Make it through the quiz, and receive a — and we cannot stress this enough — totally fake (yet well-earned) diploma.
